verses.text: Joseph fell over his father, wept against him, and kissed him. The loss hit hard. 😭
Joseph ordered his physicians to embalm Israel, and they carried it out. 🕯️
The embalming took forty days, as it normally did. The Egyptians mourned Israel for seventy days. His passing was deeply felt. 🖤
When the mourning days were over, Joseph spoke to Pharaoh’s officials: “If you’re willing to help me, please speak to Pharaoh for me—” 🙏
“—‘My father made me swear: “I’m dying. Bury me in the grave I prepared for myself in Canaan.” Please let me go bury my father; then I’ll return.’” Joseph kept his promise. 🤝
Pharaoh replied, “Go and bury your father, just as he made you swear.” ✅
Joseph went up to bury his father. Pharaoh’s officials, the elders of his household, and all Egypt’s elders went with him. 🏛️
Joseph’s whole household went too—his brothers and his father’s family. Only their children, flocks, and herds stayed behind in Goshen. 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦
Chariots and horsemen went with them too. It was a huge procession. 🐎
They reached Atad’s threshing floor beyond the Jordan and mourned with deep, intense grief. Joseph observed seven days of mourning for his father. 🖤
When the Canaanites living there saw the mourning at Atad, they said, “The Egyptians are grieving hard.” That’s why the place was named Abel Mizraim, beyond the Jordan. 🕯️
Jacob’s sons did for him exactly what he had instructed them. ✅
They carried him to Canaan and buried him in the cave at Machpelah, near Mamre. Abraham had bought the field and burial place from Ephron the Hittite. 🪦
After burying his father, Joseph returned to Egypt with his brothers and everyone who had gone up with him. The journey home began. 🧭
After their father died, Joseph’s brothers worried: “What if Joseph holds a grudge and pays us back for all the harm we did him?” Fear came rushing back. 😰
They sent Joseph a message: “Before he died, your father gave this instruction—” 💌
“‘Tell Joseph: “Please forgive your brothers for their wrong and the evil they did to you.”’ So please forgive us too, servants of your father’s God.” When Joseph heard it, he wept. 😢
Then his brothers came themselves, fell down before him, and said, “We are your servants.” 🙇
Joseph said, “Don’t be afraid. Am I in God’s place to judge you?” 🙏
“You planned evil against me, but God turned it toward good, to save many people alive—as you can see today.” Joseph named both their harm and God’s saving purpose. ✨
“So don’t be afraid. I’ll provide for you and your children.” He comforted them and spoke gently to them. 🫂
Joseph stayed in Egypt with his father’s household. He lived 110 years. ⏳
Joseph saw Ephraim’s children to the third generation. The children of Machir, Manasseh’s son, were also born on Joseph’s knees. His family kept growing. 👶
Joseph said to his brothers, “I’m dying, but God will surely come to help you and bring you out of this land to the land he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” 🕊️
Joseph made the children of Israel swear an oath: “God will surely come to help you. When he does, carry my bones up from here.” 🤝
Joseph died at 110. They embalmed him and placed him in a coffin in Egypt. Genesis closes with his family still holding to God’s promise of return. ⚰️
